overview: The Advisory Teams for Education Planning and Sustainability met to review and categorize design recommendations for the Medford High School feasibility study as it transitions into the Preferred Schematic Report phase. The groups discussed balancing academic space needs, sustainability targets, and universal design priorities for the new building.

items.title: Educational Planning, Equity, and Accessibility Recommendations
items.summary: The team reviewed a categorized list of suggestions regarding student services, special education integration, and the creation of a 'welcome center' for multilingual families. Designers clarified that items like dimmable lighting and flexible furniture are considered standard project requirements.

items.title: Toilet Room Design and Student Input
items.summary: The group discussed configurations for all-gender and binary restrooms, prioritizing privacy and safety. The committee decided to gather additional feedback through student focus groups and surveys before finalizing recommendations.

items.title: Academic Hubs and Program Adjacencies
items.summary: Members debated the placement of math labs and writing centers, as well as the integration of Career Technical Education (CTE) programs with humanities and science. Concerns were raised regarding the MSBA's classroom utilization formulas, leading to a request for the district to run scheduling scenarios.

items.title: Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA) and Carbon Modeling
items.summary: Martine Dion presented the 50-year LCCA framework required by the MSBA, which compares ground-source and air-source heat pump options against code baselines. The team discussed adopting a 30-year versus 60-year timeframe for modeling embodied and operational carbon.

items.title: LEED Certification Goals and Sustainability Workshop
items.summary: The committee addressed a discrepancy between the School Committee's Platinum certification goal and the design team's Gold target under the new LEED v5 standards. The team resolved to hold a dedicated sustainability session to evaluate the costs and benefits of higher certification levels beyond MSBA minimums.

items.title: Mechanical Systems and Temperature Controllability
items.summary: The team debated the level of local thermal control for teachers, contrasting central management with individual room thermostats. Designers recommended utilizing 'bracketed' control, allowing teachers to adjust temperatures within a predefined range to ensure energy efficiency.

items.title: Renewable Energy and EV Infrastructure
items.summary: Participants discussed the feasibility of on-site geothermal wells and the necessary electrical capacity for a future electric bus fleet. The committee will coordinate with the city's energy manager and utilities to optimize incentives for solar photovoltaic arrays and battery storage.
